A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Connected Graph|connected]] [[Definition:Plane Graph|plane graph]] with [[Definition:Dual Graph|dual]] $G^*$.
Then a set of edges $C$ is a [[Definition:Cycle (Graph Theory)|cycle]] of $G$ {{iff}} the corresponding dual edges $C^*$ form a minimal [[Definition:Edge Cut|edge cut]] of $G^*$.

B_source.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Connected Graph|connected]] [[Definition:Plane Graph|plane graph]].
The [[Definition:Cycle (Graph Theory)|cycles]] of $G$ generate its [[Definition:Cycle Space|cycle space]].

object_map.reformulation: Construct the planar dual G* (a vertex per face, an edge crossing each edge of G), swapping the roles of cycles and cuts.

validity_conditions: G must be a connected plane graph (a fixed embedding), so the dual G* is well-defined.
The bijection edge <-> dual edge carries the cycle space of G onto the cut space of G* exactly; planarity is essential (non-planar graphs have no such dual).
proof_plan: Embed $G$ in the plane and build $G^*$ with one vertex per face of $G$, and one dual edge crossing each edge of $G$.
Map each edge $e$ of $G$ to the dual edge $e^*$ crossing it.

By the [[Jordan Curve Theorem]], a cycle $C$ of $G$ separates the plane into an inside and an outside.
The dual edges $C^*$ are exactly those joining faces inside $C$ to faces outside, so they form a cut; it is minimal as both sides are connected.
Conversely, a minimal cut of $G^*$ separates the faces into two connected regions, whose common boundary is a cycle of $G$.

Hence cycles and minimal cuts are exchanged by planar duality.
{{qed}}
